title: A Solar Car and Healthy Gaming

listening1.context: You are going to hear a conversation between Muna and Sultan.

script.speaker: Muna
script.text: Hi Sultan! The science fair is next week. Have you decided on our project?

script.speaker: Sultan
script.text: Yes! I would like to build a model car that runs on solar power. It will show how the sun can give us energy.

script.speaker: Muna
script.text: That is a brilliant idea. Everybody will want to see it move without batteries. We need a small solar panel. I can order one from an online shop.

script.speaker: Sultan
script.text: That will take too long. My uncle works with solar systems, and he has a small panel in his workshop. I can ask him to lend it to us.

script.speaker: Muna
script.text: Even better, and it is free! What shall we use for the body of the car?

script.speaker: Sultan
script.text: We could use an old plastic box. It is light, and it is recycled, which fits the theme of the fair.

script.speaker: Muna
script.text: Good. How many wheels should the car have? I think we need six, so it looks strong.

script.speaker: Sultan
script.text: Six is too heavy for a small motor. Four wheels is the best number, like a real car.

script.speaker: Muna
script.text: You are right. When can we test it? We could use the science lab, but it has no sunlight.

script.speaker: Sultan
script.text: Let's test it in the school playground at noon. The sun is strongest then, and the ground is flat.

script.speaker: Muna
script.text: Good thinking. But what will happen if the weather is cloudy on the day of the fair?

script.speaker: Sultan
script.text: I will bring a strong lamp. The panel can take energy from a lamp too, so the car will still move.

script.speaker: Muna
script.text: Excellent! Remember that the fair is on Wednesday, and the judges will visit every table at ten o'clock.

script.speaker: Sultan
script.text: I know. We should make a short poster to explain how a solar panel works, because the judges will ask us many questions.

script.speaker: Muna
script.text: I will draw the diagram tonight, and you can write the explanation. Let's meet in the lab tomorrow after school.

listening2.context: You are going to hear a talk about healthy gaming.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Hello, everybody. Today I am going to talk about video games and how to enjoy them in a healthy way.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Video games are very popular. People of all ages play them, not only children, and more than three billion people around the world are gamers. The first successful video game was called Pong. It came out in nineteen seventy-two, and it was just two lines and a small ball.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Games can be good for you. Many action games improve hand-eye coordination, because players must move quickly and think fast. Puzzle games help you to solve problems. Online games with friends can also teach teamwork, because players must talk to each other to win.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: However, playing too much can cause problems. Your eyes can get tired when you look at a bright screen for a long time, and sitting still for hours is bad for your back and your body. Many gamers also stay awake late at night, so they feel sleepy at school the next day.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: So how can you play in a healthy way? Here are some simple rules. First, take a break every hour. Stand up, stretch your arms, and look at something far away for a minute. Second, on school days, play for no more than two hours, and finish your homework first.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Third, stop playing at least one hour before bedtime. Bright screens and exciting games make it hard to fall asleep. Finally, remember that you can talk to your friends away from the screen. Go outside, play sports, and meet people face to face.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Parents can help too. Most consoles and phones have settings that limit the time of play and block games that are not suitable for your age. Using them is a sensible idea.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Games are fun, but real life is better. Thank you for listening.
